title: Stream-aware latency facet dashboard and trace hooks for model-route observability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a single Grafana dashboard and associated tracing hooks that let SREs and engineers slice end-to-end inference latency by model and route with explicit streaming vs non-streaming breakdowns. The dashboard should show p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, and token throughput per model-route pairing and provide quick links to traces and logs for drilldown.

Scope:
- Metrics: ingest request latency histograms, streaming chunk latencies, request-level aggregated latency, error counters, token counts.
- Tracing: add and standardize spans: inference.request, inference.decode, inference.stream_chunk, kv.cache.lookup with consistent attributes.
- Dashboards: a facet explorer that supports variables for model, route, customer_tier, region, and streaming=true/false. Panels: time series of p50/p95/p99, stacked breakdown of service and downstream latency, waterfall sample traces, heatmap of latency distribution, and a streaming chunk latency histogram.

Telemetry sources and formats:
- Metrics: Prometheus-compatible histograms exported by runtime (metric names: rwi_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket, rwi_inference_stream_chunk_duration_seconds_bucket, rwi_inference_tokens_total). Use histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(...[5m])) by (le, model, route, streaming)) for p95.
- Traces: Jaeger/OTLP spans containing attributes: model_name, model_version, route, request_id, streaming (true/false), customer_tier, seq_length, tokens_generated.
- Logs: structured JSON in Loki with request_id for fast correlation.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Dashboard variable for streaming mode that toggles and updates panels without reloading.
2) Panels correctly surface p50/p95/p99 by model+route with streaming split visible side-by-side.
3) Clicking a point opens a trace search filtered by model, route, request_id and whether streaming=true/false.
4) Alerts: create an alert rule for sustained p95 > 800ms for high-tier models or p95 regression > 2x baseline for any model-route.
5) Tracing instrumentation PR merged with unit tests and a short migration plan for older services.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Using histogram_quantile on Prometheus histograms is cheap but requires good bucket alignment across model variants; where histograms are coarse, supplement with summary metrics for critical models.
- Streaming chunk latency has different distribution and cardinality; to avoid high-series explosion, only tag chunk-level metrics with model and route (no customer_tier) and keep chunk quantile panels separate.
- To save cost, limit high-cardinality metrics retention to 30d and keep aggregated rollups for 90d.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infr/obs/stream-latency-explorer (placeholder)
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (placeholder)
- Example Grafana dashboard JSON: attached to PR as dashboard-21421.json (will add on merge)

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Add trace attributes and metrics for 3 canary model routes and verify dashboards (1 week).
- Phase 2: Extend metrics across all runtime nodes and add alerting (1 week).
- Phase 3: Optimize bucket configs and enable rollups/retention policy updates (1 week).
